record.paper_title: Problemas abiertos en series de Fourier de Jacobi-Sobolev
record.original_question: Let w be the classical Jacobi weight on [-1,1], dmu(x) = (1-x)^alpha (1+x)^beta dx with alpha,beta > -1, and define a discrete Sobolev-type inner product by <f,g> = integral f(x)g(x)dmu(x) plus the finite sum over k=1..K and i=0..N_k of M_{k,i} f^(i)(a_k) g^(i)(a_k), with mass points a_k in (-1,1) and nonnegative coefficients M_{k,i}. Establish upper estimates for the associated orthogonal polynomials, adapting the known exterior-mass-point Jacobi-Sobolev Fourier-series methods to the interior-mass setting where the Christoffel-Darboux formulas develop singularities at the mass points.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\mu(x) = (1-x)^\alpha (1+x)^\beta\, dx$ be the classical Jacobi measure on $[-1,1]$, with parameters $\alpha,\beta > -1$. Fix points $a_1,\dots,a_K \in (-1,1)$ (interior mass points), nonnegative integers $N_1,\dots,N_K$, and nonnegative real coefficients $M_{k,i}$ for $1 \le k \le K$ and $0 \le i \le N_k$. Define the discrete Sobolev-type inner product on the space of polynomials by
$$\langle f,g\rangle \;=\; \int_{-1}^{1} f(x)g(x)\,d\mu(x) \;+\; \sum_{k=1}^{K}\sum_{i=0}^{N_k} M_{k,i}\, f^{(i)}(a_k)\, g^{(i)}(a_k).$$
Let $\{Q_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ denote the sequence of monic orthogonal polynomials with respect to $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$. Establish uniform upper estimates on $[-1,1]$ for $|Q_n(x)|$ (suitably normalized, e.g., relative to the standard Jacobi polynomials $P_n^{(\alpha,\beta)}$ and to Jacobi-type weight factors), of the type known when the mass points lie outside $[-1,1]$, but valid in the present interior-mass-point regime. The principal difficulty to be overcome is that the Christoffel–Darboux kernel associated with $d\mu$ develops singularities at the points $a_k \in (-1,1)$, which obstructs the direct adaptation of the exterior-mass-point Fourier-series methods. Provide estimates strong enough to support a convergence/divergence analysis of the associated Fourier–Sobolev series expansions.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on Jacobi–Sobolev orthogonal polynomials addresses Fourier series, Cohen-type inequalities, and relative asymptotics when mass points lie in the support of the measure, but no source located establishes the desired uniform upper estimates for the interior-mass-point case in the generality posed. The problem appears to remain open, with progress mainly in related directions (exterior mass points, asymptotics, Cohen-type inequalities).

status_evidence.title: Relative asymptotics and Fourier series of orthogonal polynomials with a discrete Sobolev inner product
status_evidence.snippet: Relative asymptotics of discrete Sobolev orthogonal polynomials when masses in the discrete part are situated within the support of the measure.
status_evidence.claim: Related work treats relative asymptotics for interior mass points, but does not provide the uniform upper estimates sought.

status_evidence.title: A Cohen Type Inequality for Fourier Expansions of Orthogonal Polynomials with a Nondiscrete Jacobi-Sobolev Inner Product
status_evidence.snippet: Cohen-type inequalities for Jacobi-Sobolev Fourier expansions.
status_evidence.claim: Adjacent results on Fourier expansions exist but in different (nondiscrete) settings.

status_evidence.title: Fourier series of Jacobi–Sobolev polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Pointwise convergence of Fourier series associated with the Jacobi-Sobolev inner product.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work on Fourier-Sobolev series exists but for the exterior or boundary mass-point case.
